title: Review and simplify the CMake build files using KISS principles
scope: Backlog item only. Review and refactoring are deferred until implementation is explicitly requested.
request: The user considers the CMake files to be in poor shape and wants them reviewed and fixed to be as simple as practical: keep it simple, straightforward, and easy to maintain.
expected: Clear, minimal CMake files that express the application's real build requirements without redundant settings, obsolete fragments, or unnecessary abstraction, while preserving supported build behavior.
implementation_notes: Review the root and test CMake files together, including how presets and build scripts depend on their options and target names.
Check minimum-version requirements, repeated settings, target structure and dependencies, QML/resource registration, platform/configuration gates, and obsolete comments or workarounds.
Prefer direct, target-based CMake and straightforward conditions. Introduce helper functions or extra files only when they make the result materially simpler.

Retain necessary complexity, especially conditional desktop keyboard resources/imports, Android packaging, test isolation, and optional model coverage. Establish why a workaround exists before removing it.
Do not combine the structural cleanup with functional app bug fixes or change public build options without identifying the need.
Update build documentation and scripts only where the simplification requires it. No specific current build failure is claimed by this maintainability report.
acceptance_criteria: Review findings and the resulting CMake structure are understandable without tracing unnecessary helper layers.
Remove proven duplication and obsolete configuration while preserving required targets, resources, dependencies, and options.
Keep the application and tests using the production QShopper library rather than duplicating model compilation.
Preserve desktop Debug/Release keyboard gating and Android's native-keyboard packaging behavior.
Preserve normal CTest execution, isolated test data/settings, and the separately optional coverage workflow.
Run tools/verify-windows.ps1 and validate additional build/configuration paths affected by the eventual changes, including Android where relevant.
Record what was simplified and any necessary complexity retained; keep the cleanup separate from functional backlog fixes.
evidence: Explicit user request to add a KISS-oriented CMake review and cleanup to the backlog on 2026-10-28.
